page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 8 shared vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration includes 300 GB of local SSD storage and does not feature a dedicated GPU. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data indicates highly competitive single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core scaling. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and single-threaded gzip compression rates placing in the top 10%. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are also strong, ranking in the top 25%. Conversely, multi-core operations, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores, align with middle-tier averages. Memory bandwidth remains consistent with average profiles, registering 87.41 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 45.45 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated physical CPU cores. However, the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-burstable multi-core execution. Given the strong single-core performance and 64.0 GB memory capacity, this instance is well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and text-processing pipelines.
